answer: Require each agent, whether composing a sonnet or routing harbor freight, to lock a $100 bond for a rolling 30-day horizon before receiving a fixed daily transaction quota. Splitting into more identities then requires proportionally more locked capital: 1,000 agents tie up $100,000. This makes Sybil scale costly without judging identity, but wealthy attackers can still buy influence, and small operators face the same entry barrier.
